question: Who won the FIRST gold medal of the modern Olympics?

post.premise: The first modern Olympic champion was a college dropout
post.bait: It was not a Greek, and it was not a runner.
post.sources_line: International Olympic Committee (olympics.com); Olympedia; Britannica; Harvard Gazette

youtube.title: Who won the first Olympic gold medal of the modern Games? Not a Greek 🥇
youtube.description:
Greece, France or the third one? The first champion of the modern Games was crowned on day one in Athens, in an event most people would not guess, and he had to quit college to get there.
Guess before the map reveals it, then see how far he jumped against a London bus and the ship route he took to the Games.
Which flag did you pick?

threads.text: Who won the first gold medal of the modern Olympics — Greece, France or the United States? Day one in Athens: the first champion in well over a thousand years was a college dropout who crossed the Atlantic on a cargo ship, and his event was not a race.

intent: The first modern Olympic champion was not a Greek and not a runner: a Boston student who quit Harvard, crossed the Atlantic by cargo ship and won the triple jump on day one — shown as a jump against a bus and a drawn sea route.

v04.text: The United States. James Connolly, a Boston student, won the triple jump in Athens on 6 April 1896.

v05.text: He hopped, skipped and jumped nearly 14 metres, further than a London bus is long.

v06.text: Harvard refused him leave to go, so he quit, and crossed the Atlantic by cargo ship to compete.

v07.text: No Olympic champion had been crowned for 1,500 years, and the man who ended the wait was a dropout.

research.topic: First champion of the modern Olympic Games: James Brendan Connolly (USA), triple jump (hop, step and jump), Panathenaic Stadium, Athens, 6 April 1896, 13.71 m; winners in 1896 received silver medals and an olive branch (retroactively counted as gold); he withdrew from Harvard after being refused leave; travelled by German freighter to Naples; first Olympic champion since the ancient Games ended in the late 4th century AD

myths.myth: A Greek runner won the first modern Olympic title.
myths.reality: The first final decided in Athens 1896 was the triple jump on the opening day, won by American James Connolly; Spyridon Louis's marathon came on 10 April.

landscape.our_gap: 1896 Shorts retell the marathon or Coubertin; nobody asks who won the very first title, shows the jump against a bus, and draws the freighter route a dropout took to get there.

ioc_1896.title: Athens 1896 Olympic Games — results and history
ioc_1896.notes: opening day 6 April 1896; James Connolly (USA) first champion of the modern Games in the triple jump; winners received silver medals and olive branches

olympedia_connolly.title: James Connolly — athlete profile
olympedia_connolly.notes: triple jump 13.71 m, 6 April 1896, Panathenaic Stadium; left Harvard to compete; also 2nd high jump, 3rd long jump

britannica_connolly.title: James Connolly — American athlete and writer
britannica_connolly.notes: first Olympic champion of the modern era; Harvard denied leave, he withdrew; travelled by freighter to Naples then train and boat to Athens

harvard_gazette.title: The first modern Olympic champion was a Harvard dropout
harvard_gazette.notes: Connolly, a South Boston son of Irish immigrants, withdrew from Harvard in 1896 after being refused leave; Harvard later offered an honorary degree, which he declined
